findings.finding: Both RBAC values are defined in R10's B1 shape. B1 drops every non-resource-URL rule unless it is bound to the loopback user (R10:obs/rbac.rs:5-7, :331-333), and I06 v4 says the snapshot does not carry such rules (HO:I4R RB06, line 197). So a ClusterRoleBinding that grants nonResourceURLs ["*"] (or /logs/*, /debug/*) to the qualification ServiceAccount, or to any other subject, leaves the rbac digest and rbacClosureDigest unchanged. The observer's role can list these rules (I4O rule 3), so under the owner's frame this is a visible part that the digest should cover. It is not a residual, and R-RBAC-COMPLETE does not name it.
findings.requiredChange: Put non-resource rules into both documents, for example as {nonResourceURLs, verbs, scope: CLUSTER} entries in each subject's effectiveRules, sorted and deduplicated like the other rules, and add a vector. The contract's document does not have to equal B1's snapshot, and Closure::check stays as it is. If the rules stay out, name R-RBAC-NONRESOURCE with a T04 check.

findings.finding: What a NetworkPolicy means depends on label selection outside the document. Its podSelector and its peers' namespaceSelector and podSelector resolve against Namespace labels and Pod labels. The observer can see Namespace labels (it lists Namespaces, I4O rule 1) but not Pod labels (no pods rule). If another namespace is relabelled to match an allowed namespaceSelector peer, ingress or egress widens, yet every NetworkPolicy byte, the agent object, the networkPolicy digest and networkEnforcementDigest stay the same. R-NET-DATAPATH's T04 check is a one-time ruleset check and does not name selector resolution.
findings.requiredChange: Choose one of two options. (1) Restrict the v1 NetworkPolicy to forms that need no selectors (podSelector {} and peers by ipBlock only) and refuse any other form. (2) Fold namespace-selector resolution into the network document, for example the name, uid and labels of each matched namespace. Either way, name a residual with its T04 check for Pod-label selection (pod labels are signer-controlled).

findings.finding: Values derived from enrollment have no live gate, so they echo the enrollment. hostPreflightDigest is the sha256 of the enrolled record: the observer reads it from a file whose pin is already in its signed configuration (R10:obs/config.rs:20-27; R10:obs/enrolled.rs:5-11). Section 5.4 sets no condition for emitting it, so as written it comes from configuration alone. Section 5.3 takes the agent object from the record with no capture check either, unlike 4.7, which requires the BROKER capture. RD:125-127 requires derivation from actual active controls and forbids loading stored values as observations.
findings.requiredChange: Emit hostPreflightDigest only while the epoch's current capture set (the role captures and the backend captures) has passed against the record. Use the NETWORK_POLICY_AGENT entry only after its backend capture passes. Give both steps a refusal text and a vector.

findings.finding: The v4 record does not have to contain backendComponents.NETWORK_POLICY_AGENT. The schema's backendComponents.required lists only APISERVER, DATASTORE, CONTROLLER_MANAGER, SCHEDULER, KUBELET and CONTAINER_RUNTIME, and backendProfile.componentKeys has minItems 6. The design does not say what happens when the entry is absent. A record with no network agent, where NetworkPolicies are not enforced, could therefore give a document with an absent or null agent, and HE-008, the release author and the observer would all compute that same value.
findings.requiredChange: Refuse when the entry, or its componentKeys member, is absent, with its own refusal text and a vector. Do the same for SERVICE_PROXY if the network document comes to rely on it.

findings.finding: The design does not name where sealedObjects comes from, and nothing binds it to the loaded hash. The ADM-4 gate proves only that the metric's loaded hash equals the configured pin (R10:obs/admission.rs:1-10). Nothing ties the eight rendered objects to that hash. The observer has no apiserver read of them (R-ADM-LIST) and no host-file read of the directory in its pinned profile. A document rendered from configuration-supplied bytes or values that differ from the pinned directory would still pass.
findings.requiredChange: Name the input: for example the four sealed values from the signed configuration, rendered by a2_objects and manifest_file_bytes, or the directory bytes themselves. Before the document is emitted, require manifest_directory_hash over exactly those bytes to equal both the signed pin and ADM-4's loaded hash. Confirm this needs no new host read, or name the read and the successor it would need.

findings.finding: Record facts. $defs.roles.BROKER requires 20 members, and the design's list leaves out interpreterPath and interpreterLabel (both const null). The 14-member choice keeps cgroup, but cgroup.inode changes per boot and per start and is OBSERVED (HO:architecture/native-profile-v4/README.md class table, line 154). That contradicts the reason given for leaving out namespaceInodes.
findings.requiredChange: List all 20 members. Either drop cgroup.inode (keeping path, the limits and selinuxLabel) or drop the boot-stability reason. Say why interpreterPath and interpreterLabel are left out, or include them.

findings.finding: Four determinism gaps. (a) Items in a served list usually have no apiVersion or kind (this is Kubernetes behaviour, not a pinned source). (b) Section 3 sorts the NetworkPolicy set by canonical bytes, but 5.3 sorts it by name. (c) 'integers must be exact' gives no bound, while VPC _bounded and R10 (obs/config.rs:7-9) both cap at 2^53 - 1. (d) The synthetic identities are not fixed as constants: 3 says synthetic cluster objects have namespace null, while PV:60-83 puts rbac and mutationBroker in the namespace, and the 4 table leaves mutationBroker's namespace open. If the observer took the names or namespaces from the binding, it would echo identity.
findings.requiredChange: (a) Take apiVersion and kind from the contract's fixed identity for each key. (b) Use one sort rule. (c) Refuse any |n| > 2^53 - 1. (d) Fix the names admissionpolicy, rbac and mutationbroker as contract constants. Set the namespace to null for admissionPolicy and to the configured qualification namespace for rbac and mutationBroker. Never read these from the binding.

findings.finding: The rbac subject set and rule set are not determined. 'ClusterRoleBindings whose rules reach it' has no definition, whereas B1 and OR03 treat every ClusterRoleBinding as reaching the namespace (R10:obs/rbac.rs:316). The design does not say which of a subject's rules are included (only scope = the namespace or CLUSTER, or all of them). It also does not say whether schemaVersion is in the rbac spec or in the closure value.
findings.requiredChange: Define the subject set and the rule set by rule (for example, every ClusterRoleBinding as in OR03, and rules whose scope is the namespace or CLUSTER). Say whether schemaVersion is included. Add a vector with a subject that also has a RoleBinding in another namespace.

findings.finding: The supersession table and reader duties leave things out. PCR:87-90 makes the seven projections release-listed files, campaigns/platform/linux-baseline/proxy-policy/<field>.json, and each <field>Digest pins that file's bytes. The design never names these files. VPO:100-106 and VPC:159-165 also require the capacity-signed preexisting references' observedDigest to equal the projection digest, so the capacity signer is a reader of this contract too. The design also does not state when the values are computed relative to I07 writes.
findings.requiredChange: Add a PCR row saying each proxy-policy/<field>.json is exactly canonical(document), with no trailing newline, and say who renders the synthetic ones. Name the release author and the capacity signer as readers. State the lifecycle: every value is computed from the sealed cluster after the policy objects exist, and an I07 write during an active binding causes refusal until new signed values exist.

findings.finding: With PPV's profile, the complete positive cannot pass VPO unchanged. VPO:90 (profileDigest), :98 (policy.<key>Digest) and :105 (the preexisting references' uid and observedDigest) bind the binding to the profile, and PPV's positive carries only sha256:1111... placeholder values.
findings.requiredChange: Have the vector carry its own profile: PPV's positive with the three uids, the seven policy digests and the three observedDigests replaced by derived values. Recompute profileDigest, bindingDigest and request.bindingDigest. Optionally also show that validate_profile accepts the profile.

findings.finding: Under host-enforcement/contracts/i01-digests-v1/, PPV's basename vectors.json collides with the contract's own vectors.json. The consumer packet is written HE-004-I01b, but R10's ids are uppercase (HE-004-I01A2, HE-004D2). validate_messages reads only the three messages, the PPV positive and CS (VPO:82-135; TPO:21-32), so PPS is not needed for the binding and observation replay. That can be decided now.
findings.requiredChange: Give PPV its own consumer path, for example beside PV under a distinct name. Spell consumerPacket the way R10 will. Record now that PPS is not read, and keep the re-check at build.

findings.finding: API-registered ValidatingAdmissionPolicies and bindings are not checked. The observer lists them (R10:obs/inputs.rs:132-137), but neither OR06 (R10:obs/operational.rs:9-11) nor the design refuses a non-static one. An object left over from before the guard loaded therefore goes unchecked. Such an object can only add denials, but live enforcement then differs from the release.
findings.requiredChange: Refuse any listed ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or binding whose name does not end in .static.k8s.io, or name this as a residual with a check.

findings.finding: The statement that no enforcement-relevant labels are used cites D1.15-1.20, which say nothing about labels or annotations. ServiceAccount's kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets annotation is what gives the included secrets list its admission meaning (this is Kubernetes behaviour, not a pinned source).
findings.requiredChange: Extend the statement to cover annotations. Then include that annotation in the ServiceAccount document, refuse when it is present, or name it as a residual with a check.

findings.finding: Some residuals are not precise enough for T04 to check. R-ONE-NP is a scope limit the observer refuses, not a part it cannot see, and it has no T04 check, which the owner's frame requires. R-DEFAULTS does not say what T04 compares. R-BROKER-LIVE does not say which document members the D1 capture leaves unobserved for BROKER. Per the NP4 class table, the process image is LABEL_BOUND, seccompFilterDigest and seccompDefaultAction are DECLARED_T04 (T04-SECCOMP-INSTALLED), and the cgroup selinuxLabel is DECLARED_T04 (T04-LABELS).
findings.requiredChange: Move R-ONE-NP to scope. Give R-DEFAULTS an exact per-kind T04 comparison, for example the spec captured at enrollment against the spec served after an apiserver restart. List R-BROKER-LIVE's unobserved members with their T04 proofs. Add residuals for D1-1 and D1-2 if those parts stay residual.

findings.finding: Fidelity. Q-DIG-10 (a), as recommended, covers networkPolicy 'unless the release needs several', and the recommendation adds 'If several NetworkPolicies are needed, (b) for networkPolicy alone'. The design narrows this to 'one in v1, a successor otherwise' without citing a fact that the release needs only one.
findings.requiredChange: Cite the fact, keep the (b) path for networkPolicy, or put the narrowing to the monitor.

findings.finding: 'Exactly one object of the kind ... named as the binding names it' can be read as 'exactly one object with that name'. Names are unique, so under that reading a second, differently named object would pass.
findings.requiredChange: Write it as two checks: the count of the kind in the namespace is 1, and that object's name equals the bound name. Give each its own refusal text.

findings.finding: No document uses the no-spec rule for Role and RoleBinding or the sorting of RoleBinding subjects, because the rbac document is in B1 shape and embeds no Role or RoleBinding document.
findings.requiredChange: Drop these rules or say where they apply.

findings.finding: The cycle analysis leaves out the record and the profile. The v4 record pins profileDigest (schema record.profileDigest; NQ:69-71), while the profile's mutationBrokerDigest comes from the record's BROKER row. There is no byte cycle only because the document contains nothing derived from the profile. The binding refers to both the record and the profile, and neither refers back.
findings.requiredChange: State this, with the order: capture, then profile, then record.

findings.finding: Q-DIG-2 (a) has the contract cite CS, PV and RD by sha256. The design says they are unchanged but does not say the contract files carry those pins.
findings.requiredChange: State that the README and definitions.json cite CS, PV and RD by sha256.

The ServiceAccount's enforce-mountable-secrets annotation removed

questions.reason: (kind, metadata.name) is a total key, because check_a2_objects S01 makes names unique (HO:AS3M). It does not depend on directory layout, and the directory hash already captures file order.
(a) is right because the cluster-wide view belongs to rbacClosureDigest, but the set must be defined by rule (D1-8): every ClusterRoleBinding as OR03 treats it, plus the rule-scope filter.
Keep the 14 members but drop cgroup.inode, which is per boot and OBSERVED. List interpreterPath and interpreterLabel (D1-6). 'The rest is in hostPreflightDigest' holds only with D1-3's live gate.
The outcome is (a), but it can be decided now: validate_messages reads only the PV messages, the PPV positive and CS, not PPS. PPV also needs a consumer path that does not collide (D1-11).
